note: Strategies that survived a research sprint (docs/METIS.md §23). Rules and summary numbers only; no market data.

entries.name: Breakout with money flowing in
entries.why: A new 20-candle high while Chaikin money flow is positive: price strength backed by closes near the highs on volume, the footprint of accumulation.

entries.name: Aroon trend start
entries.why: Aroon measures how recently the high and low were made: a fresh run of new highs with no new lows marks the start of a trend.

entries.name: New 52-week high
entries.why: Investors anchor on the 52-week high and hesitate to buy above it, so news that justifies a breakout is priced in slowly (George and Hwang 2004).

entries.name: Channel breakout (Donchian)
entries.why: Time-series momentum: assets that rose keep rising for months because news spreads slowly and investors under-react (Moskowitz, Ooi, Pedersen 2012). Buying a new N-candle high is the simplest way to ride it.

entries.name: Pullback to the 20 EMA in a stacked trend
entries.why: In a strong trend (50 above 200) prices pause at the short average and resume: continuation after a pause, the trader's 'buy the first pullback'.

entries.name: Above the Ichimoku cloud
entries.why: The cloud is a support zone from past mid-prices; a conversion-line cross above the base line while price is above the cloud is a trend continuation signal.

entries.name: Keltner breakout on heavy volume
entries.why: A close above the Keltner band on twice the usual volume says big buyers are in (institutions split orders over days, so their buying keeps coming).

entries.name: MACD turn up above zero
entries.why: A MACD histogram turning positive while MACD is above zero is momentum resuming within an established up-move, not a bottom-pick.

entries.name: Monthly calmest stocks
entries.why: The low-volatility anomaly: calm stocks have earned about as much as jumpy ones with far smaller falls, because investors overpay for lottery-like stocks (Baker, Bradley and Wurgler 2011).

entries.name: Monthly top momentum stocks (six months)
entries.why: The same anomaly over six months: reacts faster to new leaders, at the price of more trading and costs.

entries.name: Six-month momentum turning up
entries.why: Stocks that rose over the past months tend to keep rising (Jegadeesh and Titman 1993; strong in India too). Enter when medium-term momentum turns positive in an uptrend.

entries.name: Supertrend flip in a long uptrend
entries.why: Supertrend is an ATR trailing line; a flip to up inside a long uptrend is a resumed trend, while flips against the 200-candle average are mostly noise.

entries.name: Connors RSI dips in an uptrend
entries.why: Connors RSI adds the length of the down streak and how big today's fall is against the last 100 days, so it catches exhausted selling better than plain RSI.

entries.name: Short dips in an uptrend (RSI)
entries.why: Short-term overreactions reverse: forced and impatient sellers push a stock below fair value for a few days, and the buyer who provides liquidity is paid for it (Lehmann 1990; Connors). Only inside a long uptrend, where the dip is noise, not news.

entries.name: Breakout with partial profits
entries.why: Breakouts win big but rarely; selling a third at 1R and 2R banks part of the move and raises the win rate, while the rest rides the trend (scaling out, D-125).
